before.name: Question 1
before.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(1,1),(0,0),(-1,1),$ and $(0,2).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(0,-1)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(-1,0)$
before.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the linear transformation T with matrix representation T, given by T=[1−111].

The parallelogram P is mapped to the parallelogram P′ under the action of T. The parallelogram P′ has vertices (1,1),(0,0),(−1,1), and (0,2). Which of the following are vertices of P?

  1. (0,−1)
  2. (1,1)
  3. (−1,0)
a
II only
b
I and III only
c
I and II only
d
III only
e
I only
Submit

decision.explanation: T(x,y)=(x-y,x+y). I maps to (1,-1), II maps to (0,2), and III maps to (-1,-1). Only II maps to a vertex of P′. Since T is invertible (determinant 2), II is the only listed vertex of P.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(1,1),(0,0),(-1,1),$ and $(0,2).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(0,-1)$
- $(1,1)$
- $(-1,0)$
after.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1-(-1)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

EXPLANATION

First, we create a matrix Y containing all of the vertices of P′:

Y=[10−101012].

Now, if X denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of P, we have

T⋅X=YT⋅X=[10−101012].

We need to reverse the action of the matrix T. So, we multiply the above equation by T−1, and we get

T−1⋅T⋅X=T−1⋅[10−101012]X=T−1⋅[10−101012].

The inverse of T is

T−1=11−(−1)[11−11]=12[11−11].

Therefore, we obtain

X=T−1⋅[10−101012]=12[11−11][10−101012]=12[20020022]=[10010011].

As a result, the coordinates of P are (1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The quadrilateral $Q$ is mapped to the quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ has vertices $(-2,-2),(-3,2),(2,2),$ and $(-1,-1).$ Which of the following are vertices of $Q?$

- $(2,2)$
- $(0,1)$
- $(-5,-8)$
after.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${Q}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $Q$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-1-(-2)}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -8 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(0,-2),(-5,-8),(0,2),(0,-1).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

Question 3

The vector v in the plane is mapped to the vector [−21] under the action of the linear transformation T whose matrix T is given by T=[6443]. What is the original vector v?

a
[−75]
b
[−61]
c
[−57]
d
[−51]
e
[3−5]
Submit

decision.explanation: The determinant is 6·3−4·4=2, so T⁻¹=(1/2)[[3,−4],[−4,6]]. Applying this to (−2,1) gives (−5,7). Checking: 6(−5)+4(7)=−2 and 4(−5)+3(7)=1.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
after.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{18-16}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

The vector v in the plane is mapped to the vector [−21] under the action of the linear transformation T whose matrix T is given by T=[6443]. What is the original vector v?

a
[−75]
b
[−61]
c
[−57]
d
[−51]
e
[3−5]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given information, we have

T⋅v=[−21].

We need to reverse the action of the matrix T. So, we multiply the above equation by T−1, and we get

T−1⋅T⋅v=T−1⋅[−21]v=T−1⋅[−21].

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of T, which is

T−1=118−16[3−4−46]=12[3−4−46].

Therefore, the original vector is

v=T−1⋅[−21]=12[3−4−46][−21]=12[−1014]=[−57].

content.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
content.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{18-16}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -4 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
